implemented: generateStealthMeta() produces a correct provider meta-address: two random scalars (spendPriv, viewPriv) and their compressed 33-byte public keys, matching the spec 'meta-address (spendPub, viewPub)'.

deriveStealthAddress() implements the spec payer side exactly: S = ECDH(e, viewPub) via secp256k1.getSharedSecret; hS = hashToScalar(S); oneTime = spendPub + H(S)·G (ProjectivePoint.add(BASE.multiply(hS))). Returns ephemeralPriv, ephemeralPub (compressed 33B) and address (uncompressed 65B SEC1). Default ephemeralPriv is a fresh randomScalar per call.
recoverStealthSpendKey() implements the spec receiver side: S = getSharedSecret(viewPriv, ephemeralPub) — identical to the payer's S — then spendKey = (spendPriv + H(S)) mod n.

stealthAddressToEvm() maps the 65B uncompressed point to an EVM address: keccak256(address.slice(1)) then last 20 bytes, prefixed '0x'. Correct standard derivation (drops the 0x04 prefix, hashes x||y).
hashToScalar() = keccak256(data) reduced mod the curve order, never 0.
metaAddressToHex/metaAddressFromHex round-trip the two public keys as JSON hex strings.

Verified in-session: the 7 unit tests pass (npx vitest run tests/unit/core/privacy/stealth.test.ts). Node check confirmed getSharedSecret returns identical 33-byte compressed points on both sides (S equal: true), and the real test confirms recoveredKey's uncompressed public point === payer address.
testCoverage: tests/unit/core/privacy/stealth.test.ts — 7 tests, all pass: (1) meta keypair validity/lengths; (2) deterministic one-time address for a fixed ephemeral; (3) distinct address + distinct ephemeralPub per call (VAP-09); (4) receiver recovers the payer address (recovered spend key's uncompressed public point equals payment.address); (5) EVM mapping matches /^0x[0-9a-f]{40}$/; (6) meta-address serialization round-trip; (7) hashToScalar deterministic/nonzero/less-than-n. GAPS: no EIP-55 checksum assertion (and the output isn't checksummed); no negative/malformed-input tests (bad hex, wrong-length pubkeys, point-at-infinity); no fixed known-answer vector to freeze the S-byte-serialization choice (the interop risk); no assertion the recovered spend key is a nonzero scalar; nothing covering announcements/scanner (not implemented); no cross-meta per-ephemeral differentiation test.
concerns: Interop / spec-conformance (highest): hashToScalar(S) hashes the raw 33-byte compressed ECDH point as returned by noble's getSharedSecret (confirmed 33 bytes, prefix 0x02/0x03). The spec writes H(S) without pinning S's byte encoding. Any second implementation (VeilPay mobile app, backend, or the Stealth.sol / indexer referenced in the repo docs) MUST hash the same compressed-point bytes (not the x-coordinate, not an uncompressed point), or payer addresses and receiver keys will diverge. Left unspecified, this is the main correctness/interop risk.

stealth.ts:128 stealthAddressToEvm is lowercase-only but the docstring says 'EIP-55 via lowercase keccak'. EIP-55 is checksummed mixed-case; this returns an all-lowercase hex address (valid for EVM, but NOT checksummed). The x402 challenge schema (src/core/x402/types.ts:22) requires an 'EIP-55 checksummed' recipient — the comment is misleading and the output would not satisfy that stated contract.

stealth.ts:98-108 deriveStealthAddress returns ephemeralPriv inside the StealthPayment struct; the code relies on the caller manually zeroizing it ('Zeroized by the caller after use'). The ephemeral scalar is only needed to derive ephemeralPub, yet it leaves the function in a return object — an error-prone secret-lifecycle pattern for any future caller that forgets to scrub.
stealth.ts:123 recoverStealthSpendKey has no guard that (hS + spendPriv) % n != 0; a zero result would be an invalid spend key. Probability is negligible (~2^-256) but it is unchecked.

stealth.ts:94-124 No explicit input validation of spendPub/viewPub as valid on-curve points, and metaAddressFromHex (stealth.ts:145-149) silently produces wrong-length byte arrays on odd-length or non-hex input (the .match(/.{2}/g) parse can drop/merge chars) with no length assertion (compressed keys must be 33 bytes). noble's fromHex/getSharedSecret throw on malformed points so there is implicit protection, but no explicit assertions or friendly errors.
Positive note: secp256k1 has cofactor 1 (prime-order group), so there is no small-subgroup attack vector via a malicious viewPub — a real strength of the choice; not a concern.

Manual byte helpers (bytesToBigInt/bigIntToBytes at stealth.ts:60-74) reimplement endian conversion instead of using noble's utils; straightforward and verified correct by tests, but a hand-rolled primitive in crypto code. Minor.
doneVsRoadmap: The module delivers the cryptographic FOUNDATION of roadmap item 3.18 (ephemeral key, ECDH, one-time address derivation) and satisfies VAP-09 (distinct address per payment) at the crypto level (tested). It does NOT deliver the full scope. NOT done: (a) stealth announcements — no announcement type, no on-chain publish/persist mechanism; ephemeralPub is computed but never emitted or stored (spec §5 'publish ephemeralPub on-chain'); (b) stealth scanner — no scan/discovery function to identify which announcements belong to this provider (spec: 'provider scans announcements with viewPriv'); recoverStealthSpendKey exists but must be invoked per-announcement with no scan loop or matching logic; (c) encrypted notes — nothing at all in src (roadmap 3.18-3.20 'encrypted notes'); (d) x402 wiring — src/core/privacy/stealth.ts is an ORPHAN: no source file imports it (only its test), and the x402 challenge schema (src/core/x402/types.ts) exposes only a single `address` field with no spendPub/viewPub/meta-address or privacyLevel, so a provider cannot publish a stealth meta-address in a challenge and the payer cannot select stealth mode (roadmap 3.22 'Stealth x402'). (e) Stellar availability missing — spec lists 'EVM Sepolia, Stellar testnet', but only stealthAddressToEvm exists; no Stellar address mapping. The module is correctly titled 'S6 foundation' in remember.md.

implemented: Injection: manifest content_scripts match http://localhost/* and http://127.0.0.1/*, run_at document_start, all_frames:false (src/manifest.config.ts:38-46). The page-world shim (src/content/inpage.ts) defines window.veilpay as an Object.freeze object via Object.defineProperty (writable:false, configurable:false) and dispatches 'veilpay#initialized'. It holds nothing sensitive — it is a postMessage courier only: each call makes a crypto.randomUUID() nonce, stores a pending promise, posts {channel,direction:'request',nonce,kind,payload} with targetOrigin window.origin, and resolves/rejects on the matching response, mapping protocol string codes to EIP-1193 numerics via eip1193CodeFor (CHAIN_UNSUPPORTED→4902, UNKNOWN_KIND→4200) with a 30s timeout.

Agent provider: payChallenge (x402.pay), requestGrant (vap.grant.request), listGrants (vap.grants.list), revokeGrant (vap.grant.revoke), getCapabilities.

Content-script relay: index.ts checks event.source===window (iframe isolation), validates the envelope shape, gates on ALLOWED_FROM_PAGE (src/content/index.ts:18-32), then forwards to the background via chrome.runtime.sendMessage({id,v:1,source:'inpage',kind,payload}).

Router (src/core/messaging/router.ts): Zod-validates the request, enforces isPrivilegedKind vs isTrustedExtensionSurface (no tab + extension origin + UI source), and derives ctx.pageOrigin from Chrome sender.url (pageOriginFromSender) — never from the payload — before dispatching.

eth.requestAccounts (background/index.ts:387): requires unlocked vault, requires ctx.pageOrigin, never auto-grants; unapproved origins register a pending connection in chrome.storage.session and call openApprovalSurface(), returning {accounts:[]}; approved origins return the approved EVM accounts. eth.accounts returns approved addresses or [] when locked/null.

eth.sendTransaction (L437): origin + approved-address gate, pickApprovedEvmAddress (a dapp-supplied 'from' must be an approved address, else ORIGIN_DENIED; omitted 'from' falls back to first approved), parks a 'tx' approval, waits, then signs and broadcasts inside vault.withAccount (private key never leaves the SW) and returns the hash.

Grants are only ever created by the privileged 'permissions.connection' approve path, which intersects requested addresses with the wallet's owned accounts.

Approval records (connection/transaction/grant/x402-approval.ts) live only in chrome.storage.session (cleared on browser restart) and a registerLockListener cancels all in-flight waits on vault lock — nothing in these modules ever writes the durable permission/grant store.

It proves the pending record is transient and never becomes a durable grant, but it does NOT exercise the eth.requestAccounts handler wiring or the permissions.connection approve/deny path. tests/unit/core/dapp-demo-wire.test.ts — covers wire.ts: base58 round-trip, hexToBytes (0x strip + malformed rejection), and the cross-module integration where buildDemoSolanaTransfer output is accepted by the wallet's parseSolanaTransaction and signed by signSolanaTransaction (fee payer index 0, accountKeys order, ed25519 signature verification, zero-signature slot). Gap: no unit/E2E test proves a page cannot forge payload.origin, no test of eth.sendTransaction/personal.sign origin+approval enforcement or pickApprovedEvmAddress, and no test that the content-script allowlist blocks privileged kinds.
concerns: (Security, verified-negative) No path found where a page reaches a privileged operation or forges its origin. Handlers in src/background/index.ts always read ctx.pageOrigin from the router, which derives it from Chrome's sender.url (router.ts pageOriginFromSender L77-86); the inpage-supplied payload.origin (window.origin) is ignored by every security-sensitive handler (eth.requestAccounts L394, eth.sendTransaction L438, personal.sign L523, solana.* L1030/1056/1119, x402.pay L696, vap.grant.request L892). The content script also rejects non-same-window messages (event.source!==window, index.ts:68), so iframes cannot borrow the top page's relay. Privileged kinds are doubly gated: none are in ALLOWED_FROM_PAGE (content/index.ts:18-32), and even a compromised content script relay would be rejected by isTrustedExtensionSurface because content-script messages always carry sender.tab and source 'inpage' is not in EXTENSION_SOURCES (router.ts:102-112). Note pageOriginFromSender returns 'null' for about:blank/data URLs, but those do not match the localhost content-script matches, so 'null' is unreachable today.

(Defense-in-depth) Read-only enumeration kinds 'permissions.list' (background/index.ts:575) and 'vap.grants.list' (background/index.ts:863) are NOT in PRIVILEGED_KINDS — they are blocked from pages only by the content-script ALLOWED_FROM_PAGE allowlist (src/content/index.ts:18). That is a single-layer gate. If that allowlist is ever widened, a locally-served page can read the full permission table (all origin/address pairs) and all VAP grants. 'vap.grants.list' also returns grants with no origin filter (listGrants()). Recommend adding both to PRIVILEGED_KINDS so page-blocking does not rest on one allowlist.

(Correctness) Dead/unreachable API: window.veilpay.agent.listGrants() and revokeGrant() (src/content/inpage.ts:253-260) post kinds vap.grants.list / vap.grant.revoke that are absent from ALLOWED_FROM_PAGE, so they always resolve to ORIGIN_DENIED from the content script. revokeGrant is also router-privileged; listGrants is not. The exposed surface advertises two functions that can never work for a page.

(Correctness/demo) personal_sign wiring mismatch: the demo (dapp-demo/main.ts:141-152) sends its raw input string (default 'hello veilpay') as the message, but the wallet handler hex-decodes with hexToBytesStrict (background/index.ts:566) which rejects non-hex input with BAD_REQUEST. The inpage shim (inpage.ts:133) does not hex-encode either. So personal_sign with a plaintext message fails; only 0x-hex messages produce a signature (the demo's default sign button cannot complete).

(Correctness/UX) eth.sendTransaction, personal.sign, solana.signTransaction and solana.signMessage (background/index.ts:437,522,1055,1118) do not check vault-unlocked up front; eth.requestAccounts, x402.pay and vap.grant.request do. If the vault is locked on arrival, these four still park an approval and open the overlay, then vault.withAccount throws VaultLocked — which is not caught (only VaultLockedApprovalError is), so the router flattens it to INTERNAL instead of VAULT_LOCKED.

(UX consistency) solana.connect (background/index.ts:1025) throws CONNECT_PENDING when the origin is unapproved, whereas eth.requestAccounts (background/index.ts:419) returns {accounts:[]}: inconsistent pending behavior across chains for the same 'not yet approved' state.

(Performance) getApprovedAddresses (src/core/permissions/index.ts:127-136) writes lastUsedAt and calls saveStore on every read; it is invoked on each eth.accounts / eth.requestAccounts / eth.sendTransaction call, so a dapp polling accounts produces an IndexedDB write per call.

area: VeilPay Agent Payments (VAP) — grant model/service, approval decision, spend windows, audit ledger, consent-fatigue limiter
entryPoints: src/core/vap/grant.ts:createGrant / listGrants / listAllGrants / getGrantById / getActiveGrantByOrigin / revokeGrant
src/background/index.ts: handler x402.pay (~700-812), vap.grant.request (~887-950), vap.grant.resolve (~956-990), vap.grant.revoke (~872-875), vap.grants.list (~863)
implemented: Grant model (grant.ts): zod Grant with id, clientId=origin (bound at creation, checked per call), clientLabel, approvalMode literal 'autonomous' (the only mode), caps (GrantCaps), expiresAt, optional revokedAt, createdAt. Persisted as a JSON array under 'vap:grants' in IndexedDB meta store via readMeta/writeMeta — no key material, so it lives outside the encrypted vault store. Re-exports GrantCaps for existing callers.

Grant service: createGrant parses caps + expiry (GrantCaps.parse / Grant.shape.expiresAt.parse), revokes any prior ACTIVE grant for the same origin by setting revokedAt=Date.now() (one active grant per client), then pushes a new one with crypto.randomUUID. listGrants filters revokedAt===undefined (settings display). listAllGrants returns everything incl. revoked (audit path). getGrantById. getActiveGrantByOrigin matches clientId AND revokedAt===undefined AND expiresAt>now. revokeGrant is idempotent, sets revokedAt, missing id is a no-op.

requiresApproval (decision.ts) is pure. Order: revoked→deny; expired→deny; opNotAllowed→deny; chainNotAllowed→deny; overPerOpCap→deny (op.amount > BigInt(maxPerOperation)); overWindowCap→deny (spent+amount > BigInt(maxPerWindow)); threshold→required (op.amount >= BigInt(approvalThreshold)); allowlistMiss→required (allowlist non-empty and recipient not in it); else auto. Caps converted from decimal strings via BigInt at comparison point.

Spend window (decision.ts): SpendWindow {grantId, windowStart, windowEnd, amountSpent: string} persisted under 'vap:spendWindows'. loadSpendWindow returns the existing window if windowEnd>now, else writes a fresh one (windowEnd = now + windowSeconds*1000). recordSpend adds amount via BigInt sum then .toString(), starting a fresh window if the current one elapsed. Called at signing time for both auto-approved and user-approved payments.

x402.pay integration (index.ts ~700-812): gets active grant by origin; loadSpendWindow; requiresApproval; deny → appendAudit('op.denied') + throw X402_INVALID_CHALLENGE; auto → sign inside vault.withAccount('evm',0,...), recordSpend, appendAudit('op.settled', approvedBy:'grant'); required → falls through to the human prompt path (no grant, or decision required). In the user-approved path it also appends op.approved and op.settled and calls recordSpend when a grant is present.

PIN-gated resolve path (vap.grant.resolve, index.ts ~956-990): if action==='approve' → getSecurityStatus → build attempt {webauthn: payload.webauthn===true, optional pin} → requireGrantConfirmation(status, attempt) → if !ok throw BAD_REQUEST → if status.pinEnabled then verifyUserPin(payload.pin), if !ok throw BAD_REQUEST 'Incorrect PIN. The grant was not created.' Only then settle the waiter (resolveGrantApproval) and leave the grant uncreated on any failure.

WebAuthn-gated path: requireGrantConfirmation (confirmation.ts) requires attempt.webauthn===true when webauthnEnabled && !pinEnabled. The gate only checks the boolean flag (a completed-ceremony attestation is not verified); it is trusted because vap.grant.resolve is in PRIVILEGED_KINDS, enforced by the router via isTrustedExtensionSurface (sender has no tab, sender.origin === chrome-extension origin, and request.source in {popup,options,sidepanel}). getWebAuthnChallenge in security exists to issue a challenge for the UI ceremony.

Hash-chained audit ledger (audit.ts + audit-ledger repo): computeEntryHash = keccak_256 of JSON.stringify({previousHash, timestamp, operationType, sanitizedPayload}), hex-encoded. appendAudit reads tail() (repo, sorted by sequence), sequence = last.sequence+1 or 0, previousHash = last?.entryHash ?? null, entryHash computed, then putAuditEntry (validates shape, rejects empty entryHash, rejects an existing sequence — append-only). verifyAuditChain reads all entries oldest-first (readAuditEntries sorts by sequence), walks checking previousHash===expectedPrevious then recomputes computeEntryHash(expectedPrevious, record) === record.entryHash; returns {valid:false, brokenAt:sequence} on first break. exportAudit returns every entry oldest-first for export.

5-prompts/min limiter (prompt-limiter.ts): MAX_PROMPTS_PER_MINUTE=5, WINDOW_MS=60000, in-memory Map origin→timestamps. allowPrompt filters ts where now-ts<WINDOW_MS; if recent.length>=5 → returns false (auto-deny, not queued); else pushes now and returns true. Used in x402.pay fall-through path and vap.grant.request. In-memory means a service-worker restart resets it.

concerns: Caps-as-decimal-strings (src/core/messaging/protocol.ts:208,250-266; grant.ts:104): Decimal is only z.string().regex(/^\d+$/) — no upper bound (NativeAmount at :210 refines to <=MaxUint256, but GrantCaps caps do not). A page's vap.grant.request payload.caps is taken verbatim (index.ts:916-922), so a page can propose arbitrarily large caps and a 1-year window (windowSeconds max 31_536_000). The throttle is the human overlay approving the caps verbatim, plus the 90-day lifetime cap in the request schema. Also a unit-semantics drift vs spec: spec S2 says caps are bigint in 'USD-equivalent minor units'; implementation treats them as base units (wei) — the settings path converts via ethToWei (SettingsLayout.tsx:443-449) while the page path does not, so a page sending '1' means 1 wei while the settings UI sending '1' means 1 ETH. Inconsistent interpretation between the two creation paths. Lower severity (human review throttles it), but worth flagging: no sanity cap on maxPerOperation/maxPerWindow relative to a physical bound, and no cross-check that maxPerWindow>=maxPerOperation or threshold<=maxPerOperation.

Spend-window overshoot race (decision.ts:104-139, index.ts:714-738,809): the ceiling is an un-atomic check-then-act. requiresApproval reads window.amountSpent via loadSpendWindow, then recordSpend separately re-reads the full 'vap:spendWindows' array and rewrites it (loadWindows→find→{...existing, amountSpent: (BigInt+amount).toString()}→saveWindows). Halting the read and write (each its own IndexedDB op via writeMeta at storage.ts:211, a single put) means two concurrent x402.pay messages for the same origin can both read amountSpent=0, both pass requiresApproval (each individually under cap), both sign, and both recordSpend — the later write clobbers the earlier one, so the window undercounts and the maxPerWindow ceiling is overshot. The MV3 service worker does not serialize async runtime-message handlers, so this is reachable. Fix: do the read-modify-write inside one IDB transaction (or a monotonic per-grant counter) and/or read the window and record spend within the same transaction.

Audit tamper detection / 'locally signed' gap (audit.ts:1-12,66-81; spec S7:345): verifyAuditChain recomputes an UNSIGNED keccak256 over JSON.stringify({previousHash,timestamp,operationType,sanitizedPayload}). The header comment and the spec describe the ledger as 'locally signed', but there is no signature — anyone with write access to the auditLedger store (a compromised extension context, or any script running with the extension origin in devtools) can rewrite entryHash and previousHash sequentially and verifyAuditChain will report valid. Tamper-evidence protects against accidental/casual edits, not a determined local attacker. Also, every appendAudit call is fire-and-forget (void appendAudit at index.ts:720,739,786,801,874,937); if putAuditEntry rejects (e.g., sequence collision when two concurrent appends read the same tail), the error is swallowed, so a transition can be silently unlogged while the remaining chain still verifies (completeness gap on concurrency). Minor: sanitizedPayload is z.unknown() and hashed via plain JSON.stringify, so it is order-sensitive — the schema preserves key order (no transform), so re-hydration is stable today, but there is no canonical-JSON guarantee.

WebAuthn-gated path trusts a boolean flag, not an assertion (index.ts:970-975, confirmation.ts:28-33, security/index.ts:223-236): the resolve path accepts payload.webauthn===true as proof a passkey ceremony completed; it never verifies a credential assertion against settings.webauthnPublicKey. The defense is purely the router privilege layer (vap.grant.resolve is in PRIVILEGED_KINDS, checked by isTrustedExtensionSurface which requires no tab + extension origin + source in {popup,options,sidepanel}; the source field itself is forgeable but never load-bearing alone). Reasonably robust against a page, but the 'confirmation' is a UI boolean, not a verified gesture, so a bug or compromise of our own popup/options surface could create a grant with no real user gesture. Also, VAP-01 'always requires WebAuthn/PIN' is only enforced on the vap.grant.resolve path; the settings-UI createGrant (SettingsLayout.tsx:443-462) creates a grant with no requireGrantConfirmation call.

Minor: grant-approval.ts comment says expiresInSeconds is 'capped by the handler', but the cap is actually in the protocol schema (VapGrantRequestRequest expiresInSeconds max 7_776_000 = 90 days), not the handler. Minor: approvalThreshold '0' (the settings default) makes every op satisfy op.amount>=threshold, forcing required for all payments — an intentionally conservative behavior, but the property tests only assert not.toBe('deny'), which 'required' satisfies, so they don't pin an auto path in that case. No test exercises the PIN value error path ('Incorrect PIN. The grant was not created.') or the WebAuthn integration in the background handler.

Encryption: WebCrypto PBKDF2-SHA512 (600,000 iterations, 32-byte salt) → non-extractable AES-256-GCM CryptoKey; seal/open convenience wrappers; VI=12 bytes; EncryptedBlob{v:1,kdf,iterations,salt,iv,ciphertext}; DecryptionFailed is uniform between wrong passphrase and tampered ciphertext.

Key derivation (pure, no storage/globals): BIP-39 mnemonicToSeed (BIP-39 passphrase deliberately not exposed), BIP-32 via @scure/bip32 for EVM (m/44'/60'/0'/0/i, EIP-55 checksum address via keccak), SLIP-0010 ed25519 implemented explicitly for Solana (m/44'/501'/i'/0', base58) and Stellar (m/44'/148'/i', SEP-0023 strkey with CRC16-XModem). deriveAllChains derives one account per chain at an index; toAccountAddress strips privateKey.

Repositories: typed + Zod-validated access to each store (transactions indexed by from/to/network/timestamp; sessions; x402 channels by service/expiration; privacy commitments by status; walletData opaque {id,value}; audit-ledger append-only with tail + duplicate-sequence rejection).

concerns: PIN does NOT gate the vault. vault.unlock (src/background/index.ts ~291-297) uses only `payload.passphrase`; the scrypt-PIN/WebAuthn layer (security/index.ts) gates only VAP grant approval (`vap.grant.resolve`, src/background/index.ts:978-985). Weak PIN + no throttling: setupPin accepts length>=4 (security/index.ts:246-247) and verifyUserPin (security/index.ts:261) has no attempt limit/lockout. The scrypt hash+salt are stored in the `meta` store (writeMeta), readable from the same IndexedDB an attacker could dump, so a 4-digit numeric PIN (10k candidates at N=2^17 scrypt/app) is brute-forceable offline.

WebAuthn has no RP-side assertion verification: authenticateWebAuthn (security/index.ts:164) returns `credential !== null`, trusting the browser's `navigator.credentials.get` outcome without verifying the assertion signature or binding the returned assertion to the issued challenge — single-use challenge is only 'by convention'. Also registerWebAuthn (security/index.ts:125) has a redundant `response.getPublicKey() ?? response.getPublicKey()` and depends on getPublicKey(), which isn't universally supported; if it throws, the catch swallows it and registration silently returns null.

Raw key handling is enforced by convention, not by the API surface: deriveAccount (key-derivation.ts:202) and deriveAllChains (:244) are public exports returning raw `privateKey`, and mnemonicToSeed (:84) is exported. The zeroize-by-finally wipe only happens inside the index.ts wrappers (getAccountAddress/getAllAccountAddresses/withAccount). Any consumer calling deriveAccount directly (with a plaintext mnemonic) gets key bytes with no enforced wipe. Also the EVM path HDKey.fromMasterSeed(seed).derive(path) (:208-216) materializes intermediate HDNode private keys that are not zeroized — only `seed` is filled in the finally (:238).

The rule 'preimages never persist in plaintext' (storage-types.ts:59,7) is enforced by comment/convention, not schema or repository — a buggy caller could persist a preimage.

storage-migrations.ts is a marker/flag only, not a migration engine: it writes `{version:2,status:'complete',migratedAt}` into the meta store and validates it on read; the real structural migration is delegated to the native IndexedDB upgrade() in storage.ts (DB_VERSION=2). readSchemaMarker only accepts version 2, so any future version bump needs it updated, and there is no TS data-copy/transform step.

Mnemonic is materialized as an immutable string on every call: withMnemonicInternal does `new TextDecoder().decode(mnemonicBytes)` per signing/derivation, producing a fresh string copy that cannot be zeroized (JS strings are immutable). Inherent to string-based mnemonic handling; the closure copy is bytes and wipe-able, but the per-call string copies are not.

EIP-191 signing path: signPaymentPayload (payment.ts:50) canonicalizes the payload with fixed key order and no whitespace (canonicalizePayload:24), UTF-8 encodes, then signPersonalMessage (transaction.ts:197) prefixes \x19Ethereum Signed Message:\n<len>, keccak256s, and ECDSA-signs with v = recovery+27. Result {version:1, payload, signature(0x r||s||v, 65 bytes)} is base64-encoded into the X-PAYMENT header. signer is cross-checked against the recovered address.

The signer is the EIP-55 checksummed address (account.address via evmAddressFrom/toChecksumAddress); the reference server's verifyHeader recovers the signer via ecrecover and compares to payload.signer using the identical canonicalization — guarded against drift by x402-reference-server.test.ts.

concerns: REPLAY/RACE — recordSpend lost-update under-counts the window cap. src/core/vap/decision.ts:122-139 does a naive read-modify-write (loadWindows -> add -> saveWindows via readMeta/writeMeta) with no serialization, unlike appendAudit which serializes through the audit-ledger repository. In the x402.pay auto path (src/background/index.ts:712-743), loadSpendWindow reads amountSpent, then vault.withAccount awaits (signing), then recordSpend writes. Two concurrent auto-approved x402.pay for the same grant (e.g. two tabs, distinct nonces) can both read the same window.amountSpent, both pass requiresApproval, and last-write-wins drops one payment's spend, letting spend exceed the grant's maxPerWindow / bypass overWindowCap.

RACE — single-slot pending x402 record collides across concurrent payments. src/background/x402-approval.ts:13 stores under one key ('veilpay:pendingX402Payment'). Two promptable x402.pay (different origins or different challenges) both call setPendingX402Payment; the second overwrites the first's record in storage while both waiters stay alive in the in-memory map. The popup (x402.pending) renders only the last record, so resolving matches one waiter and the other silently times out after 5 minutes. Rate limiting mitigates per-origin but not cross-origin collisions.

VALIDATION/REPLAY — nonce LRU FIFO eviction can resurrect an unexpired nonce. src/core/x402/challenge.ts:17-36 evicts the oldest entry once the set exceeds 10k; an evicted nonce whose challenge is still unexpired becomes replayable within its expiry window. Acknowledged in comments as 'the server's job', but it is a real (low-probability, nonce-flood) client-side replay gap. Related: the client nonce set is in-memory only, so a service-worker restart clears it; a consumed-nonce challenge that has not expired would not be caught client-side (the server's usedNonces remains the source of truth).

VALIDATION — nonce is burned before the rate limiter, so a rate-limited payment can never be retried. validateChallenge registers the nonce at src/core/x402/challenge.ts:138, which runs before allowPrompt (src/background/index.ts:702 vs 755). A payment that is the 6th+ in a minute is auto-denied (PROMPT_RATE_LIMITED) yet its nonce is already marked seen, and the user cannot retry it until the server issues a fresh challenge.

DESIGN — resource-origin check does not bind payTo. src/core/x402/challenge.ts:107-124 only asserts that challenge.resource is same-origin with the page; challenge.payTo is constrained only to be a valid EVM address (line 103) and, when present, the grant allowlist (src/core/vap/decision.ts:79). A page running on its own origin can present a challenge with an arbitrary payTo, and the wallet will sign it. Consumer safety therefore rests on trusting the page/server plus the optional allowlist or the user prompt — worth documenting as an explicit trust boundary, not a bug.

DESIGN — payTo is never checked against an approved account, and the payer is always account index 0. x402.pay (src/background/index.ts:797) signs with vault.withAccount('evm', 0, ...) regardless of which account the user considers their payer; x402.pay does not consult getApprovedAddresses (unlike eth.sendTransaction). The overlay shows payTo, but the signer is always account 0. Acceptable for this slice but a UX/authorization gap if multiple accounts exist.

MINOR — signature s is not normalized to low-s in signPersonalMessage (src/core/chains/evm/transaction.ts:197) and the provider does not require low-s in recoverAddress; address recovery is unaffected, but low-s normalisation is standard best practice for signatures.

MINOR — signedAt is not bound to server time. signPaymentPayload defaults signedAt to Date.now() (src/core/x402/payment.ts:54) and neither the wallet nor verifyHeader (scripts/x402-reference-server.mjs) enforce a signedAt freshness/validity window; only challenge.expiry is checked. A very old signature is not rejected on its own timestamp, and provider verifyHeader also does not compare the challenge's scheme/description fields, only amount/asset/chain/payTo/nonce/expiry/resource.

MINOR — audit appends are fire-and-forget (void appendAudit) in the x402 flow (src/background/index.ts:720,739,786,801); a rejected appendAudit becomes an unhandled promise rejection in the service worker rather than being surfaced, so audit trails can silently drop entries.
doneVsRoadmap: FULFILLED (consumer side, roadmap 3.7 + VAP): 402 detection via fetch interceptor; challenge validation before any signing; EIP-191 personal_sign path yielding a base64 X-PAYMENT header; stateless provider verification mirrored by the reference server; single-use nonce replay protection client-side; VAP grant auto-approval (requiresApproval pure decision, spend window, caps, allowlist, one active grant per origin); always-prompt when no grant; consent-fatigue rate limiter (5/origin/min, auto-deny); pending record + waiter + 5-min timeout + vault-lock cancellation; privileged x402.resolve. NOT DONE / GAPS: only EVM and only account index 0 as payer; grant scoping is per-origin not per-resource (challenge.resource does not gate approval); no persistent client-side nonce store (in-memory, reset on SW restart, FIFO evict at 10k); no serialization/atomicity on the spend window (lost-update race); single-slot pending record (no per-payment queue); no backend VAP network call (VAP-07 is intentionally stateless — payments are client-signed, so 'backend replay' prevention is delegated to the provider); no test coverage for the actual background x402.pay handler wiring."

Not exploitable in production (from and key come from the same withAccount account), but it is an inconsistency and the guard provides no protection.

MEDIUM — Stellar getBalance float precision: src/core/chains/index.ts:367 does BigInt(Math.round(parseFloat(balance) * 1e7)). Horizon balance is a decimal string (e.g. '123456789.1234567'); parseFloat is float64, so stroop counts beyond ~2^53 (balances above ~900M XLM) and trailing fractional stroops can be off by a unit. Signing uses the amount directly (correct), so this only affects displayed balance, but it should parse the string to bigint stroops.

doneVsRoadmap: These modules deliver the transaction build/sign/broadcast core of the "native payment layer" for the three testnet chains: EVM Sepolia (EIP-1559, live fee estimation, EIP-1193 chain switching), Solana devnet (SystemProgram transfer + dapp signTransaction), Stellar testnet (raw-XDR native payment). They satisfy the no-heavy-SDK constraint (only @noble/@scure), the HTTP-only RPC design, and the testnet-only, permission-scoped endpoint model. Not yet done / roadmap-adjacent: mainnet endpoints (deliberately deferred and documented in TESTNET_ENDPOINTS), Solana real dynamic fee estimation (estimateGas returns a hardcoded 5000 lamports placeholder and getSequence returns 0 — both noted in comments), Stellar only supports MEMO_NONE/PRECOND_NONE/no-time-bounds (no memo or time-lock support), EVM contract deployment (to='' is rejected) and access lists (always empty), and the x402/VAP/stealth affordances that sit above these primitives. The Stellar module is the newest and most fragile because it relies on hand-encoded XDR with no SDK and no independent test anchor; it is correct today but the weakest part of the surface.
